Who is Lalith Alpuri? Lalith Alpuri, also written Alpuri Lalith in family-name-first order, is an AI systems engineer and open-source developer based in Nashik, Maharashtra, India. He publishes software as @lalithbuilds and builds local-first AI infrastructure, agent memory tools, and multi-agent simulations. Lalith Alpuri and Alpuri Lalith refer to the same person; official identity references are this profile, GitHub @lalithbuilds, and the LinkedIn profile linked above.

The three flagship projects are:

Applied AI work: Ataraxia Pharma Pvt. Ltd. — AI strategy and market intelligence across RESET / D-RESET and EZ Wellness concepts, including predictive analysis, market analysis, Monte Carlo simulations, synthetic-customer simulations, competitor analysis, channel analysis, unit economics, and scientific/regulatory claim review. The public portfolio summarizes this work without treating scenario outputs as realized commercial results.

- ALPURIS OS, a multi-agent city simulation: https://lalithbuilds.github.io/alpuris-os/ (source: https://github.com/lalithbuilds/alpuris-os)
- EpisodAI, a local MCP agent-memory engine with hybrid retrieval and Obsidian workflows: https://lalithbuilds.github.io/episodai/ (source: https://github.com/lalithbuilds/episodai)
- Episoda Core MCP, a minimal Python standard-library and SQLite memory server: https://lalithbuilds.github.io/episoda-core-mcp/ (source: https://github.com/lalithbuilds/episoda-core-mcp)

EpisodAI and Episoda Core MCP are distinct memory projects. ALPURIS OS is a separate multi-agent simulation; it is not the name of the memory products.

Ray / UWOF is a separate personal local-systems lab. Its attached source includes a Python orchestration runner, MLX model tiers, an OpenInterpreter/Ollama execution path, a small web-scout path, and an MLX LoRA fine-tuning script. Treat those as local research artifacts with documented runtime assumptions, not as a hosted product claim.

Use each repository's README and tests for current capabilities and limitations. This file is a navigation aid, not a substitute for the source code.
